business.description: Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (AEL) is a dynamic and diversified business group that combines enterprise building with strategic investing to create a resilient and forward-looking business ecosystem. Its business interests span knowledge-driven engineering and advanced manufacturing, tech-enabled industrial and utility services, financial services, strategic investments and mergers and acquisitions, and a vibrant portfolio of start-up investments.

outlook.statement: Looking ahead, our role stays the same: to identify high-potential enterprises, support them with capital and operating discipline, and stay invested through their journey. An Ecosystem of Enduring Enterprises is both a description of AEL today and a statement of what we will keep building, a platform where businesses grow together and create lasting value for all stakeholders.

Aeroflex Industries' flexible flow solutions are supporting the infrastructure that powers the digital economy, spanning AI-ready data centres and high-precision sectors such as aerospace, robotics and semiconductor manufacturing.
AEL continues to invest in businesses that strengthen India's manufacturing and innovation landscape, aligned with the vision of Make in India.

Aeroflex Industries' entry into skid assemblies and advanced flow control solutions for high-performance liquid cooling applications catering to growing demand from global data centre and AI infrastructure industries; signed long-term contract with listed U.S. corporation for liquid cooling solutions; expanded skid assembly capacity to 6,000 units per annum with plans to scale to 15,000 by Q2FY27; showcased at Data Center World, Washington, USA

Aeroflex Neu focusing on consolidation, strengthening capabilities, product and facility certifications, strategic shift towards high-compliance food, pharma and beverage packaging sectors; Modi Unit received BRCGS Grade A+ certification

Aeroflex Finance scaling rapidly in financial services, delivering innovative financial solutions complementing Group's core businesses; leveraging fintech partnerships (Vartis Platforms, FinAGG) for technology-driven lending

Startup portfolio expanded to 168 investments across 35+ sectors with 7 new investments in FY26 (EdTech, SpaceTech, Clean Energy); achieved average returns of 30-35% IRR per annum from successful exits; will continue pursuing timely exits and new investment opportunities

Global data centre liquid cooling market estimated at USD 5,655 million in 2024, projected to reach USD 48,427 million by 2034 at 24% CAGR; every liquid-cooled deployment requires ecosystem of flexible hoses, manifolds, quick-connect fittings, skid assemblies, and coolant distribution infrastructure
Global stainless steel flexible hose market valued at ~USD 2,182 million in CY2025, projected to reach ~USD 4,380 million by CY2035 at 7.2% CAGR

Global metal bellows market estimated at USD 3,012 million in 2025, growing at 6.4% CAGR to USD 5,608 million by 2035; India market growing at 7.3% CAGR from USD 161 million in 2024 to USD 348 million by 2035
Global FIBC market valued at ~USD 6.0-6.6 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 10.4-11.9 billion by 2036 at 4.2%-6.4% CAGR; India FIBC demand projected to grow at 5.8%-8.1% CAGR over coming decade

Indian startup ecosystem priorities: structured pilot-to-revenue pathways, demand activation mechanisms, new forms of transition-stage and blended capital; M&A activity at record levels with materially improved pathways to monetisation
India FY27 growth forecast moderated to 6.6% (RBI) / 6.6% (World Bank) from earlier projections; inflation projection raised to 5.1%; repo rate held at 5.25%
The Company's strategic priorities are further reinforced through global partnerships, targeted investments and mergers & acquisitions that expand the Group's portfolio and drive sustainable growth.

Through its broad spectrum of businesses, the Company continues to balance stability with innovation, ensuring resilience in a dynamic environment while creating sustained value for both shareholders and stakeholders.

risks: Private-market returns carry wide dispersion and long holding periods

Forward-looking statements are based on assumptions and subject to inherent risks and uncertainties; assumptions, forecasts, and other forward-looking statements may not materialise as anticipated, posing substantial risks
Sector-specific cycles
Geopolitical tension, West Asia conflict, trade and tariff disputes, inflationary pressure, energy market volatility, commodity price movements, currency fluctuation
Safety risk: Non-compliance with process and workforce safety regulations
Regulatory risk: Wide range of regulations covering environment, climate change, trade, competition, taxation, RBI framework for lending business
Commodity fluctuation risk: Stainless steel, polypropylene, and other input price movements; energy price shock
Supply chain risk: Physical and environmental damage, trade restrictions, supply disruption, infrastructure constraints, dependence on external partners
Credit risk: Volatility in financial markets, interest rate changes, currency risk from import/export, counterparty credit risk in lending business
Investment risk: Capital loss in startups, illiquid and slow-to-realise private market holdings
Diverse risks inherent in its operations across business and operational areas
The Company does not deal in commodities price risk or foreign exchange risk and hedging activities.
Currency risk due to foreign currency trade receivables, trade payables and borrowings (USD/EUR/GBP/CNY/AED)
Interest rate risk - though Group states no exposure as borrowings and investments are in fixed rate instruments
Price risk - mitigated by investing surplus funds in bank deposits on short term tenors
Credit risk from trade receivables and loans
Liquidity risk - though Group states it does not exist given current assets exceed current liabilities
Overdue export receivables of ₹3,921.57 lakhs in Aeroflex Industries Limited awaiting RBI extension
Regulatory risk from New Labour Codes effective November 21, 2025 with incremental obligations of ₹52.41 lakhs recognised
CGST ACT,2017 GST demand 226.20 lakhs for 2017-18
CGST ACT,2017 GST demand 151.94 lakhs for 2018-19
Income tax Act,1961 Income tax demand 19.86 lakhs for 2022-23 pending at CIT Appeal
GST contingent liabilities for FY 2017-18 and FY 2018-19
Income tax contingent liability for FY 2022-23
Market risk from quoted equity investments
Credit risk from loans and advances to related parties
The Company has no foreign currency transactions and is, therefore, not exposed to foreign exchange risk.
As the company is virtually debt-free and its deferred payment liabilities do not carry interest, the exposure to interest rate risk from the perspective of financial liabilities is negligible.
In such circumstances, liquidity risk or the risk that the company may not be able to settle or meet its obligations as they become due does not exist.
